title: Merge Intervals
statement_short: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.
hint: Interval count up to 10^4 dictates sorting by start time followed by a linear merge pass in O(n log n) time.
why_not: Right: Intervals sorting by start time allows merging overlapping adjacent ranges in O(n log n) time and O(n) space. Not Two Pointers: Scanning unsorted interval endpoints directly fails without initial sorting by start coordinates. Not Heap / Priority Queue: Storing endpoints in a min-heap takes O(n log n) time but adds unnecessary data structure overhead over array sorting. Not Greedy: Pure greedy choice without sorting by start boundaries cannot identify all overlapping interval pairs.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
